paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of clinically relevant tokens between a baseline language model, MistralV0.2-Base, and the same model fine-tuned on data from six clinical specialties. The horizontal axis represents the clinical specialty terms—Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics—listed in that order alphabetically. The vertical axis, labeled “Negative log probability,” displays a linear scale ranging from -27 to -22, with tick marks at intervals of 1. For each specialty, there are two bars: a light blue bar representing the MistralV0.2-Base model, and an orange bar representing the model fine-tuned on that specialty’s data. Within each specialty, the light blue bar consistently reaches a higher negative log probability value—for example, approximately -23.8 for Cardio and -25.5 for Pediatrics—compared to the orange bar. The orange bars representing the fine-tuned models show variation; for instance, the Gastro-tuned model consistently has the lowest negative log probability across most groups. The bars are not visibly sorted beyond their provided alphabetical order, and no bars or data points are emphasized through shading, bolding, or annotation.
